parameter_note: 2017 public parking network exceeded 13,000 spaces; 10,000 is a conservative planning availability scenario, not a current inventory.
13,000 is the 2017 public-network reference only; private-car share, party size, service rates and fleet specification are planning parameters.
Pressure scenario retains the historical parking reference but raises demand and circulation assumptions; no temporary-space total is asserted.
No current public core parking total is available; capacity is a transparent scenario bound, not a measured inventory.
1,500 corresponds to a historical operator-reported external-lot reference and is used only as a central planning scenario.
Stress scenario makes a 500-space temporary/P+R option explicit; it is recommended capacity, not an existing facility claim.
2,225 is the sum of five named ancient-city parking lots published in the 2024 tourism parking guide.
Permanent capacity is the verified five-lot ancient-city node total; other parameters are planning assumptions.
1,000 temporary spaces follows the 2023 May Day holiday expansion case and is available only in the stress/emergency scenario.
